note: Written by reference/ledgerd-client/scripts/gen-replay-conformance.ts from the TypeScript v3 fold oracle (src/replay); do not hand-edit. Each case is a log of blobs in order. An `ops` item is one blob whose body is {"v": the largest op v, "kind": "ops", "ops": [...]} (its ops are wire-canonical and may be folded directly); a `body`/`body_base64` item is a blob given as its exact plaintext body. Fold every item at its seq as sync does (decode, set aside what will not decode, fold). `expect.error` names the entry that stops the fold; otherwise `expect.state` is serializeState with every anomalies[].detail and unreadable[].reason replaced by "", and `expect.state_sha256` is the SHA-256 of that compact JSON. `expect.order` is the first-declaration order of banks and categories. `expect.diagnostics` is the oracle's own text, for reference only. See README.md.
compared: state with anomalies[].detail and unreadable[].reason blanked; order; error

cases.name: canary-v3
cases.note: The fold-fingerprint canary of replay/snapshot.ts: every v3 op type, a real fork, a duplicate ingest, a supersede, a split, an unparsed row, frozen and pending FX and a rate_unset.

cases.name: unknown-rate-null-snapshot
cases.note: conformance/fx: A transaction whose currency has no rate is saved and shown in full with a null snapshot (§3.7:132). It is not dropped, not zeroed, and not guessed at. The two rows arrive in the order t2, t1 so that the pending list below is in SORTED order rather than arrival order — the one place this suite's ordering rule is load-bearing.

cases.name: home-currency-backfills-earlier-rows
cases.note: conformance/fx: P is the smallest position >= pos(T) at which a head rate exists, so a home-currency row ingested BEFORE onboarding freezes at the identity rate the onboarding op installs. Without the backfill it would stay null forever.

cases.name: rate-live-at-ingest-freezes-there
cases.note: conformance/fx: The other side of the same rule: a rate that is already the head when the row arrives makes P = pos(T), so the row freezes at ingest rather than waiting for anything.

cases.name: later-rate-backfills-only-nulls
cases.note: conformance/fx: A later rate_set backfills every still-null row of that currency and NOTHING else. t1 and t2 both freeze at the 3.6725 head; the 4.0 head at seq 5 reaches only t3, which is sequenced after it. An executor that re-froze at the final head would report 40000 for all three.

cases.name: rate-unset-does-not-thaw
cases.note: conformance/fx: rate_unset makes later rows pending and leaves earlier freezes alone (§3.7:127). t2, ingested into the gap, waits for the NEXT rate and freezes at 5.0 — the smallest position >= its own at which a non-null head exists. A null head is a live fact, not a rate.

cases.name: rate-set-for-home-currency-is-an-anomaly
cases.note: conformance/fx: The home currency carries the implicit identity rate by construction (§3.7:124), so an op claiming a rate for it is an anomaly, not an instruction: applying it would silently re-denominate every later home-currency snapshot.

cases.name: rate-unset-for-home-currency-is-an-anomaly
cases.note: conformance/fx: The symmetric refusal. Unsetting the identity would be unrecoverable — rate_set(H) is refused and home_currency_set is one-shot — so every home-currency row after it would snapshot null forever, which §3.7:133 forbids.

cases.name: rate-set-before-home-currency-is-an-anomaly
cases.note: conformance/fx: The same rule read from the other side of onboarding. A rate for the currency that later becomes home really did apply to rows sequenced before the onboarding op — t1 is frozen at 2.0 and stays there, because §3.7 never rewrites a frozen snapshot — so the identity takes over from seq 3 and the two-basis split is SURFACED rather than left to be discovered in a total.

cases.name: supersede-recomputes-at-its-own-position
cases.note: conformance/fx: A template fix that corrects a mis-detected currency (§3.2's heuristic tier is AED-shaped). The new row is computed at ITS OWN position — AED identity — and never inherits t1's USD-based number. t1 keeps the snapshot it froze at, because a supersede is a new value at a new position, not a rewrite of an old one.

cases.name: superseded-row-is-not-backfilled
cases.note: conformance/fx: t1 was still pending when it was superseded, so it leaves the pending index with it: a retired row is not a live transaction, and a later rate_set that froze a number onto it would be freezing a number nothing displays and every re-fold recomputes differently.

cases.name: supersede-into-a-rated-currency-freezes
cases.note: conformance/fx: The other half of 'recomputes at its own position': a supersede must not be left permanently null either. t1 was pending in a currency with no rate; the corrected row lands in one that has a live head and freezes on the spot.

cases.name: recompute-carries-the-value
cases.note: conformance/fx: The 'recompute at current rate' action of §3.7:137 is a txn_edited that CARRIES the number, never an instruction to recompute later — replay stays a pure function of logged data. Setting it back to null re-arms the row for backfill, which the rate_set at seq 6 then performs.

cases.name: bigint-intermediate-exceeds-a-double
cases.note: conformance/fx: amount_minor x rate_micro is 91815912878499999, past 2^53, and the exact result sits one unit below a half-up boundary. An executor that multiplies in float64 rounds the product UP to ...500000 and reports 91815912879 — one fil too many, from a number that looks entirely plausible. The product stays below 2^63-1 so an int64 executor gets the same answer this one does.

cases.name: identity-is-exact-past-2-53
cases.note: conformance/fx: A home-currency row large enough that amount x 1000000 (9007199254740000000) is past 2^53 and NOT exactly representable — float64 puts the product at ...739999744, low by 256 — and the answer must still be the amount itself, digit for digit. Note what this does NOT pin: the 256 is six orders of magnitude below the 1000000 divisor, so the quotient survives it and a float64 executor passes this case. No identity-rate case can be a float64 guard, because diverging needs a product error above 500000, i.e. a double spacing of 1e6, i.e. a product past 2^72 — far above the 2^63-1 an int64 executor can hold at all. Cases 13 and 17 are the float64 guards; this one pins exactness at scale and the int64 bound.

cases.name: half-up-rounding-boundaries
cases.note: conformance/fx: Half-up at the boundary, in both directions, through the real fold: 1 x 1.500000 rounds to 2 and 1 x 1.499999 rounds to 1. Truncating division is half-up here only because amounts are positive by invariant (direction carries the sign), which convert() asserts rather than assumes.

cases.name: two-ops-in-one-blob
cases.note: conformance/fx: A client-authored blob carries several ops at ONE seq, so the order inside a blob is part of the total order. The rate_set and the ingest below share seq 2 with the rate first: the row freezes at ingest. Read the other way round it would be pending, so an executor that sorted by seq alone and lost intra-blob order would diverge here and nowhere else.

cases.name: float-divergence-at-the-int64-ceiling
cases.note: conformance/fx: The second float64 guard, at the far end of the magnitude range from case 13: the product is 9223368456845499999, which leaves 3580008775808 of headroom below 2^63-1 even after the +500000 — so an int64 executor computes it exactly and one built on float64 rounds the product up by 417, crosses the half-up boundary and reports 9223368456846. This is the largest conversion this suite asks any executor to perform, and it is deliberately just inside the ceiling: one rung higher and the two mandated executors would be required to disagree.

cases.name: pre-onboarding-rate-then-unset-then-onboarding
cases.note: conformance/fx: The shape that carries BOTH halves of the pre-onboarding problem at once, and which no other case reaches: a rate for the currency that becomes home, a row frozen against it, that rate then unset, a second row left pending, and only then the onboarding op — which installs the identity, backfills the pending row and raises the anomaly. t1 keeps its 2.0 basis and t2 gets the identity, so the two-basis split the anomaly reports is visible in the snapshots themselves. The anomaly fires on a NULL head, which is why the guard keys on 'a rate head exists' rather than on 'a non-null rate head exists'.

cases.name: empty-log
cases.note: No ops: the empty state, every configuration field at its default.

cases.name: sequential-recategorization
cases.note: Each edit names the head it read, so the second is an ordinary edit, not a fork.

cases.name: future-parent
cases.note: An edit naming a version beyond the head is recorded, never guessed at.

cases.name: unknown-entity
cases.note: An edit of an entity no create introduced.

cases.name: duplicate-create
cases.note: A second create of the same entity is recorded and does not clobber the first.

cases.name: entity-kind-mismatch
cases.note: An op may only address the entity kind its type owns.

cases.name: rule-and-txn-share-an-id
cases.note: Heads are keyed by (kind, id).

cases.name: fork-later-authored-wins
cases.note: Two edits from one parent: the later authored_at wins and one fork notice is recorded.

cases.name: fork-incumbent-later-authored-keeps-head
cases.note: The later-authored op wins even when it already holds the head; the challenger only consumes a version.

cases.name: fork-tie-writer-id-a-then-b
cases.note: Equal instants: the greater writer_id (UTF-8 bytes) wins.

cases.name: fork-tie-writer-id-b-then-a
cases.note: The same fork delivered in the other order resolves to the same winner.

cases.name: fork-writer-id-only-on-equal-instants
cases.note: A smaller writer_id with a later instant still wins.

cases.name: fork-sub-millisecond-is-a-tie
cases.note: authored_at is truncated to milliseconds on the wire, so these two instants tie and the writer decides.

cases.name: fork-full-tie-keeps-incumbent
cases.note: Same instant and same writer: the incumbent stays, so the fork resolves by seq.

cases.name: fork-three-way
cases.note: Three edits from one parent: two notices, the head moves twice.

cases.name: parent-zero-never-existed
cases.note: parent_version 0 names a version that never existed.

cases.name: refused-stale-edit-is-not-a-fork
cases.note: A stale-parent split that fails its sum is refused before fork resolution: no notice, no version.

cases.name: fork-on-a-rule
cases.note: Fork resolution applies to any versioned entity.

cases.name: fold-order-is-seq-not-authored-at
cases.note: The earlier-authored rate arrives later and is the head.

cases.name: duplicate-delivery-in-one-blob
cases.note: The same op twice at one seq: the second is a duplicate_delivery, not a self-fork.

cases.name: ops-in-one-blob-apply-in-order
cases.note: Every op in a blob shares its seq and applies in array order.

cases.name: seq-gaps-are-legal
cases.note: A hot-only pull sees gaps where cold rows were skipped.

cases.name: supersede-keeps-one-live-row
cases.note: The supersede retires its predecessor and becomes the one live row for the ingest id.

cases.name: duplicate-ingest
cases.note: A repeated txn_ingested for one ingest id is an anomaly, never a second live row.

cases.name: supersede-without-origin
cases.note: A supersede whose original was never seen still lands, and says so.

cases.name: supersede-chain
cases.note: Three revisions of one message; exactly one live row throughout.

cases.name: supersede-refreezes-at-its-own-position
cases.note: A supersede does not inherit the predecessor's frozen home amount.

cases.name: currency-correcting-supersede-moves-pending
cases.note: The corrected row lands in its own currency's pending set.

cases.name: fingerprint-collision-is-a-notice
cases.note: Same last4, amount, direction, merchant and UTC day: both rows stay, the later one is flagged.

cases.name: duplicate-dispositions
cases.note: Schema-v2 answers: same, different, undo; a disposition naming another row is a mismatch.

cases.name: three-way-collision-names-the-earliest
cases.note: Both later rows point at the earliest; retiring it hands the bucket on.

cases.name: possible-duplicate-is-a-snapshot
cases.note: Editing the pointed-at row out of the bucket does not re-walk the rows pointing at it.

cases.name: superseded-row-stops-matching
cases.note: A supersede with identical fields is not its own predecessor's duplicate.

cases.name: fingerprint-day-from-the-instant
cases.note: 22:00-04:00 is the next UTC day; the matching row is on that day.

cases.name: unparsed-row-materializes
cases.note: An unparsed message is a row on the review surface with no money.

cases.name: unparsed-shape-is-held
cases.note: Each payload claims unparsed while breaking one rule of the shape; only the last is the real thing.

cases.name: tier-is-a-closed-set
cases.note: template, heuristic, an absent tier (none) and an unknown one.

cases.name: parse-error-is-a-code
cases.note: A lower-snake token on an unparsed row; free text, or any parse_error on a parsed row, is refused.

cases.name: unparsed-superseded-by-a-template-fix
cases.note: A later template fix supersedes the review item into a real transaction.

cases.name: unparsed-fingerprints-are-their-own
cases.note: Two unparsed rows on one day do not collide, and an unparsed row cannot collide with a parsed one.

cases.name: edit-cannot-touch-parse-fields
cases.note: unparsed, tier and parse_error are refused on an edit; the rest of the edit applies.

cases.name: unparsed-review-flag-cannot-be-cleared
cases.note: Neither txn_categorized nor txn_edited may clear needs_review on an unparsed row; setting it true, or clearing it on a parsed row, is fine.

cases.name: unparsed-money-and-home-amount-refused
cases.note: An edit may not give an unparsed row an amount, a currency or a home amount, whoever authored the row.

cases.name: unparsed-merchant-edit-keeps-its-bucket
cases.note: An unparsed row's fingerprint is its ingest id, so a merchant edit does not move it.

cases.name: posted-at-canonical-form
cases.note: posted_at is canonicalised to UTC milliseconds; an offset that carries the canonical form out of the 4-digit-year range is refused.

cases.name: split-sum-and-replacement
cases.note: A split that does not sum is refused without a version; the corrected one applies; a later split replaces it wholesale.

cases.name: split-refused-on-unparsed
cases.note: An unparsed row has no amount to split, even an empty one.

cases.name: split-part-shapes
cases.note: Parts are positive decimal strings with a category.

cases.name: latest-checkpoint-replaces
cases.note: The latest writer_checkpoint replaces the earlier one; counters are integers past 2^53.

cases.name: checkpoint-must-be-sorted
cases.note: An unsorted or duplicated roster is refused and the previous checkpoint stands.

cases.name: home-currency-is-one-shot
cases.note: A second home_currency_set, a rate_set and a rate_unset for the home currency are all refused.

cases.name: rate-shapes
cases.note: Rates are positive decimal strings; currency codes are three letters, upper-cased.

cases.name: edited-home-amount-is-verbatim
cases.note: txn_edited carries the home amount itself, never a recompute instruction; null re-opens the pending slot.

cases.name: edit-reindexes-the-fingerprint
cases.note: An edit that changes a fingerprint field moves the row to its new bucket and clears its notice.

cases.name: money-edit-only-on-user-rows
cases.note: The ingest writer's money changes only by supersede; a row the user authored may be restated, including past 2^53.

cases.name: money-edit-reconverts-at-its-position
cases.note: A corrected amount is converted at the edit's own position; a corrected currency moves the pending bucket.

cases.name: amount-not-restated-under-a-split
cases.note: A split row's amount is frozen; its direction is not.

cases.name: edit-of-superseded-row-is-surfaced
cases.note: The edit applies to the retired row and an edit_of_superseded anomaly says so.

cases.name: edit-field-shapes
cases.note: Each malformed edit is one invalid_payload and consumes no version.

cases.name: money-shapes
cases.note: Money is a positive decimal-integer string; a JSON number, zero, a sign, a fraction or a bad direction is refused.

cases.name: category-and-review-defaults
cases.note: No category means needs_review; an empty category is no category; an explicit needs_review wins.

cases.name: provenance-comes-from-the-writer
cases.note: Only the reserved ingest writer yields provenance ingest; a payload cannot claim it.

cases.name: mailbox-message-id
cases.note: A complete mailbox provenance keeps its message id; a malformed one folds to null without an anomaly; a supersede carries its own.

cases.name: mailbox-message-id-outlook
cases.note: An Outlook provenance (a synthetic Graph immutable id) keeps its message id exactly as a Gmail one does; an empty id folds to null; a supersede carries its own.

cases.name: verified-origin-domain
cases.note: A schema-v2 field: carried on a v2 row, refused on a v1 one.

cases.name: rule-payloads
cases.note: rule_added creates and edits; its match type is a closed set and its priority an integer.

cases.name: create-and-parent-rules
cases.note: Only a create may name no parent, and a create may not name one.

cases.name: payload-not-an-object
cases.note: A payload that is not a JSON object is an invalid_payload for every op type that reads one.

cases.name: banks-last-write-per-bank
cases.note: bank_declared is last write per bank; active:false retires one; two devices adding different banks both survive.

cases.name: bank-payload-shapes
cases.note: A malformed bank_declared is an invalid_payload and leaves the set alone.

cases.name: budget-split-replaces
cases.note: Each budget_split_set replaces the whole plan, monthly total included.

cases.name: budget-split-shapes
cases.note: Whole percentages summing to exactly 100; an invalid split leaves the valid one standing.

cases.name: budget-zero-total-is-a-total
cases.note: Zero is a total a user can state; null and absent both mean no total.

cases.name: categories-last-write-per-id
cases.note: category_defined is last write per id; active:false retires without deleting; declaration order is kept.

cases.name: category-payload-shapes
cases.note: A spending category needs a bucket and the other kinds must not carry one; id, name, kind and active are required; an invalid redefinition leaves the previous one.

cases.name: unopenable-body-is-set-aside
cases.note: A body that is not JSON is set aside with its position, and the rest of the log folds.

cases.name: invalid-utf8-body
cases.note: Invalid UTF-8 is decoded with U+FFFD and then judged as JSON: here it is a valid blob whose merchant carries the replacement character.

cases.name: cold-raw-body-offered-to-the-fold
cases.note: A raw_body record is not an ops blob: it is set aside, never folded as state.

cases.name: body-shapes
cases.note: Absent and null ops are zero ops; a body that is not an object, a missing kind, a non-array ops and an unknown kind are set aside.

cases.name: wire-invalid-op-sets-aside-the-blob
cases.note: One op that fails validateOp sets aside its whole blob, including the valid op beside it.

cases.name: op-structure-refusals
cases.note: Each blob carries one structurally invalid op: an unknown type, no op_id, a bad timestamp, a missing entity, an entity with no id, a negative or fractional or unsafe parent_version, a bad ingest id, a non-object op.

cases.name: version-floors
cases.note: The configuration ops need schema v3 and the disposition v2; stamped lower, the blob is set aside rather than folded.

cases.name: authored-at-canonicalised-on-decode
cases.note: A sub-millisecond authored_at is truncated on decode; the rate's updated-at is the canonical form.

cases.name: parent-version-absent-reads-as-null
cases.note: An op with no parent_version key decodes as a create.

cases.name: newer-blob-version
cases.note: A blob from a newer schema stops the fold: it is never set aside.

cases.name: newer-op-inside-a-current-blob
cases.note: One op from a newer schema inside a v1 blob stops the fold, even though it is otherwise malformed.

cases.name: newer-configuration-op
cases.note: An op of a known type stamped with a newer schema still stops the fold.

cases.name: seq-goes-backwards
cases.note: A blob behind the folded prefix is a caller error that stops the fold.

cases.name: seq-repeats
cases.note: One blob is one row is one seq: a second blob at the same seq stops the fold.

cases.name: set-aside-blob-still-consumes-its-seq
cases.note: An undecodable blob advances the cursor, so its seq cannot be re-delivered with other content.
